templates.caveat: One input is unwired: restore_speech reads the recording from the run directory rather than from a wire, so the lane opens on an unconnected required input. Everything after it is wired, delivery included - the mastered WAV is what QC measures and what gets packaged.
templates.description: A recording the operator already has is cleaned up and mastered: cleanup, band extension back to 48 kHz, restoration, then a loudness pass and a packaged deliverable. No script is written, no voice is synthesised and no picture is made, so what comes out is the same performance, repaired.
templates.name: Audio restoration

nodes.note: The whole point of the lane, so every step is on and the gate is always rather than detected: the operator asked for repair, not for the chain to decide the take sounded fine.
Loudness only. There is no music and no sound design to bed under anything, so the music and sfx inputs stay empty and -16 LUFS is the spoken-word target rather than the video default.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: The recording. restore_speech reads it from the run directory, so the file must be in place before the run starts; nothing upstream in this lane produces audio.

templates.caveat: draft_article has no executor, which is why write_copy drafts the narration here. Everything else in the lane now runs: uploads are ingested, tables are compiled from them through declared transforms, and claims are verified against the evidence on disk.
templates.description: Sources become verified claims, claims become charted tables, and the tables become a narrated explainer over typeset cards. Research and verification run first so nothing gets said that the evidence does not carry; the voice is synthesized and measured, and the timeline is laid to the measured words rather than to a guess.
templates.name: Data story video

values.topic: what a public dataset actually shows

nodes.note: Optional, and the place to start. Drop files in <project>/uploads and they are sniffed by magic number, stored immutably and recorded as operator_upload sources. A CSV or JSON lands as a dataset in compile_datasets; put a <file>.transforms.json beside it to declare how to shape it. With an empty uploads dir this is a no-op and research finds its own sources.
Deep, not standard. An explainer is only worth making if the sourcing survives a reader who checks it.

Re-verifies every claim against the evidence and datasets on disk, and enforces the independent-source requirement: a high-stakes claim carried by two outlets that both credit the same wire has ONE publisher behind it. The script's own gate is at lock_script, where there is a script to gate.

Uploaded CSV/JSON to typed tables through declared transforms, which is what makes a chart reproducible rather than drawn. A table read straight from a file is SOURCE_DATA; one whose transforms computed a value is DERIVED_DATA, and the renderer labels the difference. With no uploads it falls back to the sample table so the lane still runs.
Seven beats rather than five. A claim needs setup, number and consequence, so an explainer runs longer than a short.
The narration draft. Direct because a documentary voice states the finding and stops.
Freezes the words so the measured timings stay valid. Both the plan and the copy draft are wired; the copy is what gets spoken.
Slightly under speed so a listener can carry a number from one sentence to the next.

values.instruct: calm documentary narrator, unhurried, no hype

nodes.note: Gated on detected artifacts by default, so a clean take passes through untouched.
Not optional in this lane. A number said aloud has to be readable too.
The documentary mood and the -18 dB bed are already the defaults, so nothing is set here.
No sound_design in this lane. Foley over charts is decoration, and it competes with the one thing the viewer has to hear.
One typeset still per beat. The card count follows the run's deliverable spec, not a widget, so the cards widget is deliberately left unset.
Cached per card, so fixing one number re-renders one card. The images stay as the thumbnail and carousel set; qc_deliverable reads the card bundles back for accessibility.
Milliseconds to whole frames against the measured narration, which is why it runs after align_words rather than after the story.
Checked against the archive after the cut, so a rerun of the same topic is caught before packaging rather than after publishing.
The last gate looks at what would actually be shipped, not at the master it came from.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: A topic in the brief, and the sources it should be held to. Numbers must arrive as tables (CSV/JSON), not as prose, or there is nothing to chart. Music is picked from the local library at fixtures/music; an empty library selects no bed rather than failing.

templates.description: One script becomes one narrated timeline whose beats are drawn two different ways: data scenes are rendered deterministically as typeset cards, staged scenes are generated from Blender controls through the image and video models, and the two are spliced back together in beat order. Narration is synthesized, aligned, captioned and mixed once for the whole film.
templates.name: Hybrid video

values.topic: how something works, told with its own numbers

nodes.note: Beats, each with a scene kind. The kind is what route_shots later reads.
An even pace matters here because the beat boundaries are taken from these timings.

values.instruct: calm explanatory narrator, unhurried, even pace

nodes.note: Polish only. Synthesized narration has no room noise or band limit to repair, so cleanup and band extension stay off. Same length out as in, so the timings below stay valid.
No sound design in this lane. Data beats have nothing to foley and mixed sources would.

No fps value: the story's own rate is master and the stage takes it from the plan. It was pinned to 24 here "to match plan_shots", which is how the wind shorts shipped 24 fps footage in a 30 fps film — the pin matched the planner's default, not the script.
Charts, maps, tables and titles. The beats routed to render are cut from this.
One shot per beat, camera preset following the scene kind.

Written down here rather than left to a setting. `image` is the only scene kind with no text in it, so it is the only one an image model can draw without garbling something a viewer is meant to read; titles, quotes, charts and tables are typeset. Add a kind here, or one beat at a time through routing.overrides, when a film needs it.
Headless Blender writes the control passes, so staged beats keep one continuous space.
No text in the image on purpose. Anything a viewer is meant to read belongs on a rendered card where it is typeset rather than drawn.

values.prompt: the scene staged exactly as the control passes show
values.style: one consistent editorial illustration look across every staged beat, restrained palette, clean shapes, no photographic lighting, no text or numerals in the image

nodes.note: No size value. With a shot plan the clip is generated at the ShotSpec's own size — what the anchor was drawn at and the control passes were rendered at. `size` is read only on the `motion: hold` path. compose_video letterboxes into the timeline frame, never crops.

values.prompt: camera moves exactly as staged in the 3D scene

nodes.note: Takes the routing as well as both picture sources, so each beat is filled from the branch it was routed to and the film comes out in beat order rather than branch order.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: A script with at least one `image` scene: that is the kind the router sends to the generative chain, and the demo fixture has none, so it routes nothing. The worked example is `--story fixtures/story/wind_2024.json --shots fixtures/shots/wind_2024.json` (eight beats, two of them images, 30 fps, 9:16). If the script must be researched first, use data-story-video.

templates.caveat: The set is fixed at the 8 frames of the builtin control plan, and its per-image layout is that plan's hand-gesture fixture, not the views the brief asks for. generate_keyframes declares a frames widget the runner does not read, so you cannot yet ask for a number of images or say what each shows.
templates.description: Several images of one subject that have to match. An anchor image fixes the look, a generation lock freezes the model, seed, sampler and style prompts around it, and every later image is edited from the anchor under that lock rather than generated fresh. Drift QC measures how far each image moved from the anchor, a person signs off the sheet, and the set is packaged as one deliverable.
templates.name: Image set

nodes.note: The list of views, as beats. Point its story widget at a written fixture when the views are decided in advance rather than drafted.

The one image the rest of the set is measured against. The seed is pinned because the lock freezes it and every later image reuses it; which number does not matter, that it holds between runs does. No model value: _reference_backend() reads the image_sequences.backend setting and never this node, so a model here would name a weight it does not pick.

values.prompt: the subject alone, centred, plain background, the reference view of the set
values.style: consistent character and material design, even flat lighting, no dramatic shadow, plain neutral background, same rendering idiom in every image

nodes.note: Model, seed, sampler and the style, camera and lighting prompts, frozen around the anchor.

Per-image layout, from the builtin 2D plan. The compiler is set explicitly rather than left to its widget default because the stage falls back to the controls.compiler setting when the node is silent, and a settings change would otherwise reroute this lane through video.
Hub and spoke: every image is an edit of the anchor under the lock, never an independent generation. Frames that fail the drift thresholds are regenerated here before drift_qc sees them.
Reads the per-image drift records: how much of the locked region survived and how far the style moved. This is the stage that answers whether the set actually matches.
Drift is a number. Whether the set looks like one set is a judgement, so a person makes it.

The readable form of a set: every image at thumbnail size, judged as one sheet. There is no format value to set: contact sheet, mp4 flip-through and flipbook PDF are all written every time, and the widget that looked like a choice has been removed from the node rather than left on the canvas doing nothing.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: A brief naming the subject, and the look written out on generate_anchor (prompt plus style). The set is only as consistent as that anchor, so draft the anchor prompt before running. What each later image shows is not yet yours to choose - see the caveat. For real images image_sequences.backend must be hidream; the default mock backend draws placeholders.

templates.caveat: Every stage here has an executor, but two inputs are unwired on purpose. generate_anchor gets no STORY because this lane has no script, so it draws the first frame from the brief topic and its own prompt instead. And no node type ingests a supplied still, so starting from an image you already have is not expressible in the graph today.
templates.description: A single still becomes a short moving shot. The anchor fixes the opening frame, LTX-2.5 invents the motion out of it, frame interpolation smooths the result, and QC and packaging turn the clip into something deliverable. No script, no voice, no cut between shots.
templates.name: Image to video

nodes.note: Unwired because generate_anchor reads a STORY, not a BRIEF. The runner still takes the topic from here.

values.topic: one image brought into motion by a slow camera push

nodes.note: The first frame the whole clip grows out of. No style is frozen here: the look belongs to the shot the operator asked for, not to the lane.

values.prompt: the opening frame of the shot, as it should look before anything moves

nodes.note: With no shot plan the runner prompts from the brief topic and sizes the clip from the anchor, so keep this prompt saying the same thing as the topic rather than fighting it.

values.prompt: hold the framing of the first frame and let the motion develop out of it

nodes.note: The quality tier, not the fast one. One short clip is cheap enough to interpolate well, and a camera push is where the fast tier's warping shows.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: A subject written into the brief topic. With no shot plan in the run, the runner takes both the anchor prompt and the motion prompt from that topic, so it is the one field that has to be right. A starting image of your own cannot be wired in yet; see the caveat.

templates.caveat: The first stage takes no wire. upscale.frames is a required input left unwired on purpose: the operator's images are read from the run directory rather than handed over by an upstream node, so the graph starts from a slot the canvas shows as empty. Every stage in the lane has an executor.
templates.description: Images that already exist are restored and enlarged, then checked and packaged for delivery. SeedVR2 does the work one frame at a time, so the lane is indifferent to whether the folder holds photographs, drawings or rendered stills. Nothing is generated: the output is the input at a higher resolution.
templates.name: Image upscale

nodes.note: Frame by frame over the stills, so a folder of pictures is one job. 2160 rather than the 1080 default because enlarging is the errand. The runner reads the resolution from settings.postchain.upscale_resolution today, so a local run needs that set to match.
An upscaler can smear a face or invent texture, so the enlarged set is looked at before it ships.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: The images to upscale, staged in the run's input frame directory. This lane produces no material of its own, so with no pictures in place there is nothing for it to do.

templates.description: A written script becomes a narrated video of typeset cards. Text to speech reads the beats, the measured beat lengths set the card timings and the captions so both follow the real voice, and the timeline is rendered deterministically. There is no generative imagery, so a rerun of the same script produces the same film.

models.label: Kokoro skill env, for the lighter alternative voice

templates.name: Narrated video

values.topic: a written script read aloud over typeset cards

nodes.note: Optional, and the only way a picture gets into this lane. Files in <project>/uploads are sniffed by magic number, stored immutably, recorded as operator_upload sources and carried into the render bundle as assets - which is what an image, screenshot, map or background still resolves against. With an empty uploads dir this is a no-op and the film is cards only.
The script. Set the story widget to the fixture path; plan_story freezes a written plan here rather than drafting one.
One spoken sentence per beat, frozen before anything is voiced or timed.
Synthetic voice, because this lane exists for scripts nobody has recorded. Swap voice for kokoro-82m for a faster read, or use the voice_over stage instead if takes exist.
The FFmpeg tail only: de-esser, EQ and light compression. The neural cleanup and enhancer steps stay off, since a TTS take has no room noise or band loss to repair.

A gate, not the aligner: the word timings are written by synthesize_narration (its aligner widget), and this stage validates them - coverage, overlaps, drift - and fails the run before captions or card timings are built on a bad take. Card duration comes from the measured beat lengths, so the voice sets it either way; this is what stops a silently mistimed one.
Cues ship as a sidecar even when the cards already carry the text.

Nothing is set: stage_select_music reads no widget values, so both mood and gain_db are inert here and the bed always lands at its built-in -18 dB under the voice. An empty music library selects nothing, which is the usual state of this lane - the words are the whole content.
Measured beats become scenes, so card duration comes from the voice and not from a guess.
Remotion renders the typeset cards from the compiled timeline.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: A written script as a StoryPlan fixture (fixtures/story/<name>.json), named on the story node's story widget. Left empty, plan_story falls back to the built-in sample plan, which is useful for a smoke run and nothing else. Real narration needs the TTS skill env and weights below; the default mock voice runs offline.

templates.caveat: The length of the cut is fixed at the 8 frames of the builtin motion plan, so you cannot yet ask this lane for a specific number of pictures. generate_keyframes declares no widget for it, which is honest rather than helpful: the count comes from the control plan.
templates.description: A brief or a written story becomes one anchor picture, then a whole sequence held to that picture, then a silent clip. The generation lock freezes model and seed so the frames cannot drift apart, drift QC throws out the ones that wander anyway, a reviewer looks at the contact sheet, and ffmpeg cuts what survives. There is no voice and no music on this lane.
templates.name: Photo sequence video

values.topic: a place changing over a day

nodes.note: One beat per picture. A written story fixture skips the drafting entirely.
The look of the whole film is decided once, here, and nowhere else.

values.prompt: the opening picture of the sequence, the frame every later one is judged against
values.style: consistent illustration, one palette, one light direction, flat even composition, no text, no borders

nodes.note: Model, seed and controls frozen. Without this the sequence is a pile of related pictures.

The compiler is pinned rather than left silent. stage_compile_controls falls back to the global controls.compiler setting when the node sets nothing, and on the blender compiler generate_keyframes and drift_qc both skip themselves - which would leave compose_video with no frames to cut. This lane has no 3D scene anyway; scene-controlled-video is the variant where Blender stages the shots.

No frames value is set, because the runner does not read one: stage_generate_keyframes takes its length from the builtin motion plan, which holds 8 frames. Setting the widget would look like it chose the length of the cut and would not.
Frames that stopped looking like the anchor are regenerated before anyone sees them.
A machine measure of drift is not the same as a person looking at the contact sheet.

Frames only: the audio and captions inputs stay empty, and the cut comes out with no audio stream rather than a silent one. The approved PNGs are cut at 8 fps into exports/generated.mp4 — this lane has no generate_video to make a picture for it.
Slideshow detection matters more here than anywhere else, since a held sequence really is a slideshow and the report has to say so rather than fail it.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: A brief, or a written story at fixtures/story/<name>.json named in the story node's story fixture widget. The pictures are drawn by this lane, so there is nothing to record or supply.

templates.description: A written or drafted script becomes staged 3D shots, then drawings, then a film. Blender holds the cinematography and the bodies so the same characters appear shot after shot; the image model draws the look; LTX moves between the drawings or holds them. Your own recording carries the voice.

models.label: Baked mocap clip library (two-person CMU contact)

templates.name: Picture story

nodes.note: The script. plan_story freezes the written story rather than drafting one.

Asks the reference library, in the beat's own words, for the real interaction to stage from. affection: affection is the setting that keeps a shove out of a tender scene; half the labelled material on disk is aggression. With no library on disk this selects nothing and the lane still runs.

One 3D shot per beat, each staged from the mocap clip retrieval chose, so the contact on screen is contact that was captured rather than contact that was guessed. A beat with no match falls back to the preset staging. Pass --shots to override the whole plan with a hand-authored fixture, e.g. fixtures/shots/two_hander_mocap.json.
Nothing is drawn from a character nobody has looked at.
Headless Blender writes the control passes the drawing is conditioned on.

values.prompt: the two of them, staged exactly as the control passes show
values.style: hand-drawn ink and watercolour illustration, confident brush line, flat washes, paper texture, consistent character design, no 3D render look, no photographic lighting

nodes.note: Rejecting one drawing costs one drawing, not the film.
motion: hold turns the same lane into held drawings; ltx animates between them.

values.prompt: camera and characters move exactly as staged in the 3D scene

nodes.note: Ignored on a held cut, and deliberately so: with motion set to hold the stage sees the hold marker, skips itself and records skipped="held cut". Interpolating held drawings invents frames nobody drew or reviewed, which destroys the one property that mode exists for. So both values can stay set and switching motion to hold still gives a held film.

No format value: the stage writes the SRT, the WebVTT and the styled ASS burn-in track every time, because the sidecars cost nothing and compose_video burns from the SRT. It used to carry `format: srt`, which the executor never read.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: A script (fixtures/story/<name>.json) and, for voice_over, recordings under takes/. Without recordings, swap voice_over for synthesize_narration.

templates.description: A story becomes staged 3D shots, then control passes, then anchor images, then a film. The 3D scene owns the camera and the blocking so shots stay consistent and repeatable; HiDream draws the look conditioned on the passes; LTX-2.5 moves between the anchors along the staged motion. Picture only, no narration or music.
templates.name: Scene-controlled video

values.topic: a place changing over one afternoon

nodes.note: The beats. One 3D shot is staged per beat, so the beat list is also the shot list.
Camera path, framing and frame count per beat. Left on the story presets so the plan follows the writing; point planner at a fixture when a shot list has already been decided by hand.
The blocking is checked before any passes are rendered, because every later stage inherits it.
Headless Blender renders depth, normals, segmentation, skeleton and a rough RGB. The pass set is left at its default because the anchor stage wants all of it.
One anchor per shot keyframe, conditioned on the passes rather than on a described camera.

values.prompt: the scene exactly as the control passes stage it, held in one consistent look
values.style: cinematic practical-camera photography, natural light, shallow depth of field, filmic grading, physically plausible surfaces, no video-game gloss, no illustration

nodes.note: Anchors become the first frame and the LTX keyframe guides, so the motion the model invents is bounded by the staged one. Landscape, unlike the portrait default.

values.prompt: camera and bodies move exactly as staged in the 3D scene

nodes.note: Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: A story to stage (a fixture under fixtures/story/, or a brief for plan_story to draft from) and a working Blender with the scene controller's assets, since compile_controls renders the passes headlessly. A shot plan can be supplied instead by setting plan_shots.planner to fixture.

templates.description: A story plan becomes shots, drawings and motion, and the finished cut carries music and sound effects but no speech. Nothing in the picture is timed to a spoken line, so the lane can also be run with the sound stages removed, which delivers a silent cut. It cannot make narration, and it writes no captions.
templates.name: Silent video

nodes.note: The beats exist to order the pictures, not to be spoken.

The default 2D motion plan, not Blender. No dialogue means no repeated speaking characters to keep consistent, which is the one thing that earns the 3D staging cost. Set compiler to blender when the material does need staged bodies.
With nothing said, the frame has to carry the meaning on its own.

values.prompt: the scene as the shot plan frames it, no text and no on-screen words
values.style: one consistent look across every shot, composed to read without narration, strong silhouette and clear subject, no captions, no lettering

nodes.note: motion: hold instead cuts the drawings as held stills, which suits a slower silent piece.

values.prompt: unhurried motion that reads on its own, camera and subject as the shot plan stages them

nodes.note: The bed is the only thing under the picture, so it is chosen to sit there for the whole cut rather than to fill gaps between lines.
Louder than the -22 dB default: that default keeps effects under narration, and here there is no narration to stay under.
With no voice the music is the base and the effects bed on top of it, both looped to the picture's length and mastered to the delivery level. Nothing ducks, because there is nothing to duck under.
No captions input: nothing is said, so there is nothing to caption. Drop music and foley too and this writes a video-only cut with no audio stream at all.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: A brief, or a written script in fixtures/story/<name>.json set on plan_story.story. For music, a local music library manifest under the music library dir; select_music picks nothing when it is empty rather than failing.

templates.caveat: compose_video's frames input is left unwired on purpose: this lane makes a clip, not a frame sequence, so the picture arrives on clips and the composer picks it up from the run directory. The publish node is the canvas terminal; the runner stops after the destination packages.
templates.description: A brief becomes one short vertical clip that is ready to post. The image model draws the frame, LTX moves it, the narration is synthesized and cleaned, word timings drive the captions, MMAudio writes the sound under the voice, and the mixed cut is checked and packaged per destination.
templates.name: Single clip post

values.topic: one thing worth watching for eight seconds

nodes.note: Three beats, because one clip cannot carry five and still land.
The script is frozen here so the word timings the captions use stay valid.
No recording in this lane, so the voice is generated from the locked script.

values.instruct: close, level delivery, no announcer lift at the end of a line

nodes.note: Synthesized speech is clean until it is not. The gate stays on "detected", so restoration only runs on beats where the detector hears an artifact.
SRT, which compose_video burns in. Posted clips are watched with the sound off.
The one frame the motion pass grows from, so the whole clip inherits its look.

values.prompt: the subject of the brief, one clear vertical frame, nothing else competing for the eye
values.style: photographic, single strong light, shallow depth of field, muted palette, vertical framing with the subject off centre, no text, no logo, no collage

nodes.note: 9:16 at six seconds. One generation is the whole picture; there is nothing to cut to.

values.prompt: slow push in on the subject, small real movement in the frame, no camera shake

nodes.note: MMAudio watches the clip. Speech and music are excluded so the bed stays under the voice.
Narration with the sound bed ducked under it, mastered to the -14 LUFS the platforms want.
Checked against the archive before anything is packaged. A block here is not overridable.
Destination and profile are chosen per run, and the post is approval gated. The runner skips this node: it marks where the packages go.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: A topic on the brief, or a written script as fixtures/story/<name>.json set on plan_story's story widget. Nothing needs recording: the voice is synthesized. Posting needs a distribution profile.

templates.description: A brief becomes one finished still. plan_story turns the topic into a single beat, the image model draws it, and the delivery pair checks the file and writes the per-destination crops. There is no motion, no audio and no consistency machinery here, so nothing carries over to a second image.
templates.name: Single image

nodes.note: One beat, because one beat is one image. More beats would plan frames nothing draws.
model is the only thing that used to fork this lane into two workflows. krea2-turbo draws the same graph; megapixels is left at its default because hidream-o1 ignores it.

values.prompt: the subject of the brief, framed as a single finished picture
values.style: one clear subject, deliberate composition, even readable lighting, no collage, no panels, no text overlay

nodes.note: The image itself is the deliverable, so QC reads it rather than a cut.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: Only the brief: a topic on the brief node and a prompt on generate_anchor. Drawing with Krea2 instead of HiDream also needs the optional ComfyUI weights below.

templates.caveat: Nothing loads an existing video, so the entry frames are not a wire: fix_video reads whatever the run directory already holds. Removal is also a no-op on its own, because Cutie needs a Blender segmentation seed mask under controls/, which only a lane that ran compile_controls writes. Upscale, interpolation and QC do run standalone.
templates.description: A video or frame sequence that already exists, finished: tracked objects inpainted out of every frame, SeedVR2 restore and upscale, interpolation to a higher frame rate, then QC and the destination packages. Nothing in the lane invents picture or sound, so it is the one to run on footage from another lane, from a camera, or from a render made outside this repo.

models.label: Post chain tools (Cutie, ProPainter, SeedVR2, GIMM-VFI)

templates.name: Video finishing

nodes.note: The entry. Its frames come from the run directory, not from a wire. remove_ids and mask_dilation are read from settings.postchain today, not from these widgets, so setting them here would not change the run.
Resolution comes from settings.postchain.upscale_resolution, default 1080. 1440 and 2160 are offered but the 7B model at that size is tight on a 24GB card.

The quality tier, not the fast one: this lane exists to finish a picture, and the frames are already final, so the slower interpolator is worth the wait. rife is the fast tier and none leaves the cadence alone, which is what a held-drawing cut wants.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: The material to finish, already in the run directory: exports/generated.mp4, per-shot video/<shot>/clip.mp4, or a frame sequence at sequence/frames. Removal ids come from settings.postchain.remove_seg_ids.

templates.description: A written script becomes a clean spoken track with measured word timings and a caption file. The voice is a real recording, restored rather than generated: cleanup and band extension where the take needs them, then Resemble Enhance. No picture is made at any point, and the chain cannot change a word's timing, so the captions describe the audio that actually exists.
templates.name: Narration track

nodes.note: The written script, frozen into beats. Beats are what a take and a caption are keyed by.
The words stop moving here, so alignment and captions measure one fixed text.
Measured timings, not apportioned ones. even_split spreads a beat's duration across its words, which is fine under pictures and wrong when the timings are part of the deliverable.

voice_over normalises every take to 16 kHz mono for alignment, so band extension is what puts the top octaves back before delivery. The gate stays on detected, unlike the repair lane: a take recorded for this script is usually clean. cuda because nothing else wants the GPU here and the enhancer is about 19x realtime on CPU.
Where the run's files land. Not a step - the deliverable folder is written either way - but the lane's last output has somewhere to go, and the canvas can stop calling it unused.

templates.prerequisite: A written script for plan_story to freeze, and one recording per beat under takes/, named by beat id. A missing take fails voice_over and names the beat rather than filling the gap.
